## REVISED SCOPE — applied after adversarial review

Two additions land in F1:

1. Client locale-transport. Add an axios request interceptor in the i18n module that reads the active locale from localStorage (ai-novel-locale) and sends it as Accept-Language on every request. This is the client half of the locale-transport contract; F2 adds the server middleware half. Without this, the server cannot know locale for any global/server string or pre-novel prompt. Verified: apiClient.create at client/src/api/client.ts:17 currently sets baseURL/timeout only.

2. index.html boot strings. client/index.html has a Chinese title (line 9: AI 小说创作工作台), a Chinese boot heading (line 73: 正在加载创作工作台), and boot copy (line 74). These render BEFORE React mounts, so react-i18next cannot reach them. F1 must localize them — either via a tiny inline script that reads localStorage and swaps the text before mount, or via Vite transformIndexHtml. Document the chosen approach.

3. Owned module requirement. F1 MUST establish a single owned module client/src/i18n/ (config, resolver, locale-transport interceptor) that U1-U4 feed into. Per Architecture Rules, do NOT scatter per-page translation dictionaries as loose files — all locale JSON lives under client/src/locales/ and all logic under client/src/i18n/.

### Revised acceptance criteria (add to original)
- axios interceptor sends Accept-Language from the active locale on every request
- index.html title + boot copy localize correctly in both zh and en before React mount
- client/src/i18n/ is the single owned i18n module; U1-U4 locale files all live under client/src/locales/

BRANCH: feature/english-translation. Per-phase commit required.
## ROUND 2 REVIEW — APPLIED to F1

### SHOULD-FIX — Accept-Language contract pinned (F1 and F2 must agree)
F1 and F2 run in parallel by different agents. To prevent divergence, pin the contract:
- Header name: Accept-Language
- Value: bare token, exactly "zh" or "en"
- F1 axios interceptor reads localStorage ai-novel-locale and sets the header to that bare token on every request
- Server (F2) normalizes: trim, lowercase, unknown values fall back to "zh"
Both F1 and F2 reference this contract.

### NIT — line ref
Original said apiClient.create at client.ts:17. Actual axios.create is around line 17-22 (line 17 is the export, line 22 the call). The baseURL/timeout-only claim is correct; just the line number is approximate. No action needed beyond awareness.

### SHOULD-FIX — react-query cache invalidation on locale switch
When the user switches locale mid-session, the Accept-Language interceptor only affects NEW requests, so stale old-locale server strings linger in the react-query cache (genre tree, story-mode seeds, labels) until refetch. F1's locale switcher MUST call queryClient.invalidateQueries() or queryClient.clear() on locale change (QueryClient lives at client/src/main.tsx:13). Add to F1 acceptance.

### Branch serialization note
F1 runs parallel with F2 and F3 on feature/english-translation. Use a bd merge-slot gate for the P1 trio, or a per-issue branch merging into feature/english-translation, to avoid concurrent-commit races.
## ROUND 3 REVIEW (FINAL) — APPLIED to F1

### BLOCKER — locale-transport must cover fetch(), not just axios
The Accept-Language interceptor from round 2 only covers axios. But streaming endpoints — the PRIMARY chapter-production path — use raw fetch() with only Content-Type, so the locale never reaches the server for chapter generation / Creative Hub chat. Verified: useSSE.ts:108, creativeHub.ts:103, AssistantChatPanel.tsx:212.

F1 acceptance MUST extend the locale-transport contract beyond axios. PREFERRED approach: create a shared locale-header helper (e.g., client/src/i18n/localeHeaders.ts) that returns the Accept-Language header from localStorage; consume it in BOTH apiClient's axios interceptor AND all fetch callers (useSSE, creativeHub, AssistantChatPanel). One helper, all callers, no drift.

### SHOULD-FIX — desktop IPC write side belongs to F1
Round-2 put the desktop main-process locale store in U4, with U4's note saying "F1's locale switcher writes to this store via a NEW IPC channel". But F1's notes had ZERO mention of desktop/IPC. F1 is P1 (first wave), U4 is P2 (depends on F1) — F1 could close without creating the IPC channel, leaving U4's main-process i18n with no locale source.

F1 acceptance MUST add: the locale switcher also writes the active locale to a main-readable store (desktop/src/runtime/locale.json under userData, or electron-store if installed) via a NEW IPC channel (preload.ts bridge + main.ts handler). This is the F1-to-U4 contract. Note: electron-store is NOT currently a dependency and no reusable userData store pattern exists (verified desktop/package.json + desktop/src/runtime), so F1/U4 must either install electron-store or write a small fs JSON helper — decide and document.

### Branch serialization
F1/F2/F3 parallel on feature/english-translation — use bd merge-slot gates (verified real command) or per-issue branches merging into feature/english-translation.
## DISPATCH-READY (planner-authored, verified)

- [ ] `client/src/locales/zh/` + `client/src/locales/en/` JSON exist (Home page keys populated). react-i18next initialized; `<App>` wrapped in `I18nextProvider`.

- [ ] SHARED locale-header helper `client/src/i18n/localeHeaders.ts` returns the `Accept-Language` header (bare token `zh`|`en`) from `localStorage` consumer contract. Consumed by: axios interceptor in the i18n module AND all fetch callers (`useSSE.ts:108`, `creativeHub.ts:103`, `AssistantChatPanel.tsx:212`). One helper, all callers, no drift.
- [ ] axios interceptor sets `Accept-Language` on every request.
- [ ] `client/index.html` title (L9 `AI 小说创作工作台`) + boot copy (L73-74) localize correctly in both zh and en BEFORE React mount (inline script reading localStorage, or Vite `transformIndexHtml`).

title: i18n-F2: Prompt locale routing foundation + genre example
notes:
## REVISED SCOPE — applied after adversarial review (supersedes original acceptance criteria where they conflict)

The review found that Novel has NO language field and there is no locale-transport between client and server. Two additions land in F2:

1. Novel.language migration (additive). Add a language String @default zh column to the Novel Prisma model (schema.prisma ~L307). This is the locale source for NOVEL-SCOPED prompts only. Additive migration only — never destructive; do not reset data.

2. Server locale middleware. Add Express middleware that reads the Accept-Language header (sent by F1's axios interceptor) and exposes req.locale (zh default). This is the locale source for GLOBAL/PRE-NOVEL prompts.

3. Genre example rewire (CORRECTION). The original body said genre generation reads novel.language. That is INFEASIBLE: the /generate endpoint body is prompt/provider/model/temperature/maxTokens with NO novelId, and genre-tree generation happens BEFORE any novel row exists (verified routes/genre.ts:46-52). So the genre example must use the CLIENT-SUPPLIED locale from req.locale (the middleware), NOT novel.language. Novel.language is reserved for novel-scoped prompts wired in P2.

4. Call-site count correction. Original said ~198 runner call sites; actual is approximately 120. The no-import-change conclusion still holds — callers keep importing the zh asset as anchor; the runner swaps to the en variant when options.locale differs and a variant exists.

### Revised acceptance criteria (replace original)
- Registry key changed to id@version@language (zh + en coexist; no Duplicate prompt asset registration crash)
- PromptExecutionOptions gains optional locale field
- resolvePromptVariant(id, version, locale) helper with zh fallback + warning on miss
- runStructuredPrompt + runTextPrompt swap to resolved variant when locale differs
- PromptWorkbench still resolves correctly after key change
- Novel.language column added (additive migration; default zh) — novel-scoped locale source
- Server Accept-Language middleware added exposing req.locale — global locale source
- ONE English prompt variant created: genre.tree.generate@v1@en (domain-aware rewrite)
- Genre call site wired to pass options.locale FROM req.locale (NOT novel.language, since genre is pre-novel)
- Test: locale en renders English genre variant; locale zh renders Chinese; zh byte-identical regression; fallback warns when missing
- pnpm --filter server build passes

FILE SCOPE additions: server/src/prisma/schema.prisma (Novel.language column + migration), a new small middleware file for Accept-Language parsing (owned under server/src/app or platform middleware, NOT a loose utils file per Architecture Rules).

BRANCH: feature/english-translation (per AGENTS.md branch workflow). Per-phase commit required before merge to beta.
## ROUND 2 REVIEW — APPLIED (3 reviewers, fix-first; findings re-verified by planner)

### BLOCKER (confirmed) — streaming prompts bypass the resolver
Round-2 found that streamTextPrompt (promptRunner.ts:864) and streamStructuredPrompt (:955) are the PRIMARY chapter-production path, called 4x in novelCoreGenerationService.ts (112/176/305/380) + chapterWritingGraph.ts:292 + ChapterRepairStreamRuntime.ts:116. F2's original acceptance only covered runStructuredPrompt + runTextPrompt, so en variants would never reach chapter generation.

VERIFIED FIX (better than per-runner swaps): all 4 runners funnel through preparePromptExecution (:250, called at :701/:810/:879/:971). Put the locale swap INSIDE preparePromptExecution — one edit covers all 4 runners including streaming. This is cleaner than 4 separate swaps.

### Revised F2 acceptance — ADD these
- The locale-aware resolvePromptVariant swap MUST be implemented inside preparePromptExecution (not per-runner), so runStructuredPrompt, runTextPrompt, streamTextPrompt, AND streamStructuredPrompt are all covered by one change
- Test: streaming path (streamTextPrompt or streamStructuredPrompt) with options.locale=en renders the English variant; with zh renders Chinese; zh byte-identical regression
- The genre example still uses runStructuredPrompt (fine as a smoke test), but the swap location is preparePromptExecution so the streaming path is verified too

### SHOULD-FIX (applied) — Accept-Language contract pinned
F1 and F2 run in parallel by different agents; without a pinned contract they could disagree. Pinning now: header name is Accept-Language; value is a bare token (zh or en); server normalizes (trims, lowercases, maps unknown to zh); fallback is zh. Both F1 and F2 reference this contract.

### SHOULD-FIX (applied) — branch serialization
F1/F2/F3 are parallel (no inter-deps) but all pin feature/english-translation — concurrent commits race. Resolution: use bd merge-slot gates for the parallel P1 trio (F1/F2/F3) so only one lands at a time, OR each agent works on a per-issue branch merging into feature/english-translation. Note added to F1/F2/F3.

### SHOULD-FIX (applied) — schema.prisma serialization between F2 and S2
F2 (Novel.language) and S2 (NovelStoryMode.language + CreativeHubThread backfill) both edit schema.prisma and are not currently chained (S2 depends on F1+F3, not F2). Add explicit F2-before-S2 sequencing for schema.prisma edits, or a merge-slot gate. Adding dep S2-depends-on-F2 for the migration collision.

### Note on the 198 number
Round-2 caught that the PRD parent note still says 198 in two places while F2 corrected to ~120. The parent note could not be updated via bd CLI (backticks shell-interpreted). The verified count is ~120 (119 raw). Recorded in bd memory i18n-prd-review-applied. F2 carries the authoritative count.
## ROUND 3 REVIEW (FINAL) — APPLIED (2 fix-first, 1 publish; findings re-verified by planner)

Round 3 confirmed the streaming FIX is technically sound (preparePromptExecution swap is feasible) BUT found a compounding transport gap that defeats it, plus an internal contradiction.

### BLOCKER (confirmed) — streaming endpoints use fetch(), not axios
Round-2's Accept-Language interceptor only covers axios. But the PRIMARY chapter-production path and Creative Hub chat use RAW fetch() with only Content-Type — no Accept-Language. Verified: useSSE.ts:108 (chapter/bible/beats/repair generation), creativeHub.ts:103 (Creative Hub chat), AssistantChatPanel.tsx:212 (chat). So even with the preparePromptExecution swap, the locale never reaches the server for streaming — chapter generation stays Chinese.

F1 acceptance MUST extend the locale-transport contract beyond axios: either (a) centralize Accept-Language injection inside useSSE (read localStorage, set header on the fetch at useSSE.ts:110) AND patch the two standalone fetch sites (creativeHub.ts:103, AssistantChatPanel.tsx:212), or (b) create a shared locale-header helper consumed by BOTH apiClient and all fetch callers. Option (b) is cleaner — one helper, all callers.

### SHOULD-FIX — resolve F2's internal contradiction (consistency)
F2's REVISED SCOPE still has the stale bullet "runStructuredPrompt + runTextPrompt swap to resolved variant when locale differs" (per-runner swap) coexisting with the ROUND 2 bullet "swap MUST be inside preparePromptExecution (not per-runner)". An implementer following the stale bullet would re-introduce the streaming blocker. STRIKING the stale per-runner bullet. Authoritative F2 acceptance: the resolvePromptVariant swap happens ONCE inside preparePromptExecution, covering all 4 runners.

### SHOULD-FIX — locale logging for diagnosability (completeness)
PromptInvocationMeta has no locale/variant field (promptTypes.ts:70-96); logPromptCompletion doesn't emit it (:284-319). title: PRD: Internationalization (i18n) — Multi-Language Support for the AI Novel Production Engine
notes:
## Risk clarification (Phase 3)

Updated the Phase 3 risk framing based on review. The original PRD overstated risk by conflating two distinct concerns. The corrected picture:

### Two different risks, clearly separated

**Risk A — System integrity (does Chinese still work?)**
With proper locale isolation, this risk is near-zero for all phases:
- Chinese prompts stay in their files, untouched
- English prompts are NEW  variants registered alongside
- Registry resolves by locale — Chinese requests never touch English code
- Chinese regression snapshots guard against accidental drift

**Risk B — English output quality (does English produce GOOD novels?)**
This is a content/craft risk, independent of the i18n architecture. An English prompt can be perfectly registered, correctly routed, fully isolated from Chinese — and STILL produce mediocre English novels, because Chinese prompts encode domain knowledge (web-novel pacing, Chinese genre taxonomies like 玄幻/修仙/都市, narrative voice). Translating to English is not a string swap; it's a domain-aware rewrite for English fiction conventions (three-act structure, Western genre categories).

### Corrected risk matrix

| Phase | Break-Chinese risk (A) | Quality risk (B) | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Docs | Zero | Low | Medium |
| 2. UI i18n | Near-zero | Low (bad translation = ugly label, easy to fix) | High (voluminous) |
| 3. Prompts | **Near-zero** (i18n protects this) | **High** (English prompt tuning is a craft effort) | **Highest** (labor) |
| 4. Completeness | Near-zero | Low | Medium |

### Key insight
Phase 3 is the most LABOR-INTENSIVE phase (crafting and tuning 120 English prompt variants), but it is NOT the most DANGEROUS. The i18n architecture fully protects Chinese. The only "risk" is that English novels will need prompt tuning to reach the same quality bar as Chinese — which is an iterative content effort, not a system-integrity concern.

The small architectural touch in Phase 3 is changing the registry key from  to . That change is testable and containable — if routing breaks, you get the wrong variant (caught by tests), not corrupted output.

### Corresponding User Story update
User story #28 ("As a Chinese-speaking user, I want all AI prompts to produce identical output to today — no quality regression in Chinese novel generation") is now classified as a Risk A guard (system integrity), protected by locale isolation + regression snapshots.

User story #22 ("As an English-speaking user, I want the AI to generate novels in English when I select English") carries an implicit Risk B note: the English variants will work immediately but may require iterative tuning to reach Chinese-quality output. This should be tracked as follow-up quality debt per prompt family, not as a blocker for Phase 3 completion.

The original Implementation Decision ("change registry key to id@version@language; runner passes locale; registry falls back to zh") was PARTIALLY INACCURATE. Verified facts from the code:

2. **The registry's  key is NOT used for runtime routing.** It is used by the PromptWorkbench and lookup helpers (, etc.).
